speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, such as whether it is intermittent or constant, and if you experience any weakness, numbness, or vision changes. Additionally, could you list the significant medical conditions and medications from your history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of feeling "drunk" and clumsiness on the right side suggest an issue with your cerebellum or its connections. Do you notice any double vision, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your speech pattern, such as slurring? Additionally, are you currently taking any new medications or have you had any recent head injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, which carries a significant risk for PML, especially with the onset of cerebellar signs, the diagnosis is highly probable. I will proceed with ordering specific imaging and tests to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST TEST: CSF Oligoclonal bands and JC virus PCR.
